cards.explanation: The answer is that the LORD will rule over them. Gideon, Israel's leader in the fight with Midian, hears the offer: rule over us, you, your son and your grandson. He says, “I will not rule over you, nor will my son. The LORD shall rule over you.” (Judges 8:23) Offered a crown, and he hands it right back, friends. Meanwhile I can't even turn down the last cookie on the cooling rack.

The answer is True. Gideon asks, and the Israelites answer, “We will give them gladly…” Then they spread out a garment, and each man throws an earring from his plunder onto it. Gladly, friends. I've seen people hold onto a cookie harder than that, and I was one of them.

The answer is Ophrah. Gideon placed the ephod in Ophrah, his hometown. Hold on to that spot, friends, because the very next words tell us what happened there. The verse says all Israel worshiped it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his household. (Judges 8:27)

The answer is snare. The text says the ephod “…became a snare to Gideon and his household.” A snare is a trap that catches you. All Israel ended up worshiping it there, and that's the trouble. Sometimes the thing that grabs your ankle is the one nobody saw coming.

The answer is rest. The text says, “So the land had rest for forty years in the days of Gideon…” Midian was subdued and never raised its head again. That's forty years with no Midian at the door. Forty years of rest is longer than I've ever gone without burning at least one batch.

The answer is that he had many wives. The text says, “Gideon had seventy sons of his own, since he had many wives.” Seventy sons is a lot of birthdays. That's a lot of names to remember, and I'm the guy who forgets which drawer he put the spatula in. Hold on to this number, friends, because those sons come up again.

The answer is at a ripe old age. The text says, “…Gideon son of Joash died at a ripe old age…” He was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of the Abiezrites. A long life, and he's buried in his father's tomb.

The answer is that they turned to the Baals. The text says, “…as soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites turned and prostituted themselves with the Baals…” The Baals were false gods. “…as soon as…” is the part that stings, friends. Earlier the Israelites offered Gideon rule, and the moment he was gone they turned to the Baals.

The answer is True. The verse says, “The Israelites failed to remember the LORD their God who had delivered them from the hands of all their enemies on every side.” He had delivered them, and they didn't remember it. It's like forgetting who baked the batch while you're eating the cookies. Friends, that's a hard thing to read.

The answer is False. The verse says, “They did not show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) for all the good things he had done for Israel.” Jerubbaal is Gideon's other name. After all the good he did for them, his house got no kindness. I think that one hurts.
